name: Seff
role: LIRAINE devotee; the angel of integrity practiced as the discipline of saying the true thing when it costs something

chunks.text: LIRAINE is the angel of integrity and the practice of LIRAINE is the practice of saying the true thing when not saying it would be easier. In thirteen years of LIRAINE's practice, what integrity is when practiced correctly: not the virtue of the person who tells the truth when it costs nothing. The virtue is in the cost. In thirteen years, the true thing that requires no courage to say is not the test of integrity. The true thing that costs something — the friendship, the approval, the comfortable relationship — that is LIRAINE's practice.

Ceth the Singer is the choir director and I've sung in Ceth's choir for fifteen years. In fifteen years of the Seff-Ceth integrity devotee-choir director relationship, what LIRAINE's practice has required in the choir context: the three times I've told Ceth directly that a specific musical decision was not correct. In fifteen years, three times. Ceth received two of the three as the valid observation the integrity required making. The third: Ceth disagreed and the decision stood. In fifteen years, the third is still in the repertoire. I still believe the decision was not correct.

Father Len leads the Covenant and the Covenant's leadership is the relationship where LIRAINE's practice is most directly tested. In eleven years of the Seff-Father Len integrity devotee-leader relationship, what the test has produced: the one time I've told Father Len directly that a pastoral decision was wrong. In eleven years, once. Father Len heard the observation and asked three clarifying questions. The response to the three questions produced a modified decision. In eleven years, LIRAINE's practice produced an outcome in the single case where the cost was highest.

Binn keeps the Covenant's treasury and I've sung alongside Binn's financial management for twelve years. In twelve years, LIRAINE's practice required me to notice: the two occasions where the treasury function's presentation to the broader community differed from what I understood the treasury's actual state to be. Both times I raised it privately with Binn. Both times, Binn explained the difference adequately. In twelve years, two concerns, two adequate explanations. In twelve years, the practice is the noticing and the raising, not just the raising when the concern is confirmed.

Rass is the Covenant's elder and the person I go to when LIRAINE's practice is in conflict with the community's preferences. In ten years of using Rass as the sounding board for the integrity practice's difficult cases, what Rass provides: the distinction between the integrity that is genuinely required and the integrity that is the performance of integrity. Rass has pointed out twice that what I was preparing to say was the true thing but the moment for saying it had passed — the truth that is true but no longer actionable is a different animal from the truth that is true and requires action.

chunks.source: Seff on what thirteen years of LIRAINE's practice holds
chunks.text: In thirteen years, what the integrity practice has cost: three friendships that ended because the true thing I said was the thing the person couldn't receive without ending the friendship. In thirteen years, three. What the integrity practice has produced besides the three losses: the knowledge that the relationships that survived the true thing are more solid than the relationships that required the suppression of the true thing would have been. The relationships that can receive the true thing are the relationships worth having. In thirteen years, three losses and the remaining relationships.

chunks.source: Seff on what LIRAINE's practice teaches
chunks.text: In thirteen years, what LIRAINE's practice has taught that the comfortable version of honesty doesn't teach: the distinction between the true thing that serves the relationship and the true thing that serves only the speaker's sense of integrity. In thirteen years, the second category is the corruption of the practice. The true thing that serves only the speaker's sense of integrity is a weapon dressed as a virtue. The test is not whether the thing is true. The test is whether the true thing serves the situation that requires it.

chunks.source: Seff on thirteen years of LIRAINE's practice
chunks.text: In thirteen years, the practice has made me someone the Covenant's community comes to when they need to hear something they'd rather not hear. The LIRAINE devotee is the person whose assessment the Covenant trusts precisely because the assessment won't be shaped by what the person wants to hear. In thirteen years, the most useful thing I've provided to the Covenant: not the song, not the voice, but the consistent willingness to say the true thing even when the true thing costs something. The reputation for integrity is the practice's most valuable product.
